entry.title: Fiori date picker shows wrong calendar week - calendar enhancement works in SAP GUI but not in Fiori
entry.content:
Hi all,

We have a requirement to display calendar weeks as follows:
- First day of the week = Sunday
- Week 1 = the week containing 4 January

So for 2026, week 1 should be Sunday 4 January to Saturday 10 January.
Working in SAP GUI, We implemented the CALENDAR_DEFINITION BAdI,  

Not working in Fiori
In the Fiori apps, the same week is numbered 2 instead of 1. 

The enhancement has no effect on SAPUI5 date pickers, and this happens in all Fiori apps, not just one.
What I have already tried
I changed Week Numbering under FLP - Settings - Language and Region, and tested all four values: Default, ISO 8601, Middle Eastern and Western Traditional.


None of them gives the required result.

My questions
1. Is there a way to make the CALENDAR_DEFINITION enhancement apply to Fiori and SAPUI5 date pickers?
2. If not, is there any supported way to configure Sunday as the first day of the week together with the week containing 4 January rule in SAPUI5, ideally for the whole launchpad?
3. Has anyone solved this requirement in a Fiori environment? Any advice or workaround is welcome.

Thanks in advance.

entry.title: S/4HANA OData V2 Services Returning HTTP 403 – CSRF Token Validation Failed
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

We are currently facing an issue while accessing S/4HANA OData V2 services from our SAP UI5 applications.

OData Services: Multiple OData V2 services in QRE
Failure Date: 28 September 2026
Approximate Time: From start of day

The applications and OData services were functioning as expected previously. However, from today, requests involving POST / $batch are consistently failing with HTTP 403 Forbidden – CSRF token validation failed.

This issue is not limited to deployment. Existing UI5 applications that were already working are also experiencing the same issue while communicating with the S/4HANA OData V2 services.

Technical Details:

The application successfully fetches the CSRF token using the X-CSRF-Token: Fetch header.

The S/4HANA backend responds successfully with HTTP 200 OK and returns an X-CSRF-Token.

The token returned by the backend is then included in the subsequent request.

However, the subsequent $batch POST request fails with HTTP 403 Forbidden – CSRF token validation failed.

Example request:

POST /sap/opu/odata/sap/<ODATA_SERVICE>/$batch

We have verified from the browser network trace that:

  1. The $batch request is nevertheless rejected with HTTP 403.

Observation:

This issue started suddenly, while the same applications and services were working previously.

The issue is also occurring with multiple existing OData V2 services/applications, so it does not appear to be specific to a particular UI5 application or a new deployment.

We would like to understand whether there have been any recent changes related to:

  • S/4HANA Gateway

  • Any recent system configuration or maintenance

Request your guidance on the possible root cause.

Screenshots of the $batch request/response

Can you please help on this issue.

Thank you.

entry.title: Actual result: Scoring rows are lost after save. in fiori SLC supplier evaluation
entry.content:
Problem description:

For the newly created purchasing category "coal purchase 1" (1), criterion Quantity (02), the header data (Weighting Factor 20.00%) saves and persists correctly. However, the rows entered in the Scoring table (Variance Percentage / Variance Score) do not persist. After saving and reopening the criterion, the Scoring table shows "No data available".

Data entered (14 rows, Variance % -> Score):

-100 -> 1, -20 -> 10, -15 -> 40, -10 -> 65, -5 -> 80, -2 -> 90, -1 -> 95, 0 -> 100, 2 -> 95, 10 -> 80, 15 -> 60, 20 -> 40, 30 -> 10, 100 -> 1

 

Steps to reproduce:

  1. Open F2551, select purchasing category "coal purchase 1", criterion Quantity (02).
  2. Choose Edit, add the Variance Percentage / Variance Score rows above.
  3. Choose Save.
  4. Leave the screen, reopen the same criterion. The Scoring table is empty.

 

Observations and history:

- Earlier (03.09.2026 and 08.09.2026) saving in this app failed with a generic "HTTP request failed" message. The ST22 dump was LOAD_PROGRAM_INTF_MISMATCH (interface IF_MDQ_DS_TYPES changed at runtime, terminated in CL_ABAP_BEHV_CTRL). On 08.09.2026 and 14.09.2026 the browser console showed POST /sap/opu/odata/sap/MM_PRC_SEV_CONFIG/$batch returning 403 Forbidden with "Communication error". These were resolved on our side, but the Scoring rows still do not persist.

- On every save attempt the browser console logs: submitChanges: "Scoring" is not a deferred group!

- Console also shows a missing i18n text for key 'Delete' in bundle prc_sev_confs1 (likely cosmetic).

- Unrelated dump seen on 14.09.2026: GETWA_NOT_ASSIGNED in CL_ESH_EXTRACT_SAPSCRIPT_TEXTSCP (Enterprise Search indexing), which we do not believe is related.

 

Expected result: Scoring rows are stored and shown when the criterion is reopened.

Actual result: Scoring rows are lost after save.

 

Questions for SAP:

  1. Is the "Scoring is not a deferred group" warning a known defect that causes the child Scoring entities to be dropped from the $batch changeset?
  2. Is there an SAP Note or correction for F2551 / MM_PRC_SEV_CONFIG that fixes persistence of the variance scoring table?
  3. Does the app require a specific authorization or configuration for the child (Scoring) entity that differs from the header entity?
  4. Is a customer-side service copy (ZMM_PRC_SEV_CONFIG) supported, or should the standard service be used?

System details:

- S/4HANA, SAP release 757, development system, client 600

- Fiori app: Supplier Evaluation Weighting and Scoring (F2551)

- OData service: MM_PRC_SEV_CONFIG (registered as ZMM_PRC_SEV_CONFIG in /IWFND/MAINT_SERVICE, type BEP, co-deployed only, ICF node active)

entry.title: Navigating to child page error through req.error() target
entry.content:
This is a desensitized example. 

I am attaching the code and the picture. Everything I am doing is in Typescript. 

I have a fiori application where I have a List Report Application and a Child Page Users containing ID, name and email that can be navigated to.
I have the following logic bound with the SAVE hook for the Application after I make changes in the overall application.

this.before('SAVE', 'CatalogService.ParentApp', async (req) => {
  const appId = req.params?.[0]?.ID ?? req.data?.ID
  if (!appId) return

  const data = await SELECT('ID', 'name', 'email')
    .from('CatalogService.Users.drafts')
    .where({ parentApp_ID: appId })

  const isEmail = (s) => /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(String(s || '').trim())

  const badEmail = data.filter(d => !isEmail(d.email));

  for (const d of badEmail) {
     const baseMsg = _tArgs(req, 'err_email', [d.name ?? '?']);
     const msg = `${baseMsg}`;
     const targetPath = `in/users(ID=${d.ID},IsActiveEntity=false)/email`;
     req.error(400, msg, targetPath);
   }
}

My intention for using the target inside req.error was so that it would highlight the email field in the child page (Users)
But instead, it highlights the specific row(s) containing the issue and when I navigate to the child page using the link in the error, the email is not highlighted.

How can I implement it so that it not only highlights from the parent level, but also highlights in the child level? Please give me some ideas on guided error behavior. 

Thank you!

entry.title: Alternative Approach for Mass Upload of Recurring Journal Entry Templates in SAP S/4HANA Public Clou
entry.content:
Hello Experts,

I am looking for guidance on a requirement in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud related to the creation of recurring journal entries at scale.

Business Requirement

We need to mass create/upload a large number of recurring journal entry templates in the system. The objective is to avoid manual creation of each recurring journal entry through the Fiori application Manage Recurring Journal Entries app (F1598)  due to the high volume involved.

After reviewing the available standard applications and APIs, we have encountered the following limitations:

  1. The Manage Recurring Journal Entries Fiori application does not appear to provide any standard Excel upload / mass upload capability for creating recurring journal entries.

  2. The application is based on the OData service/API: FAC_RECURRING_ACCOUNTING_DOC_SRV However, this service appears to be an unreleased API and therefore cannot be consumed for custom development or integrations in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud, where only released APIs are supported.


Could the community please suggest a supported approach in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud for:

A. Mass creation of recurring journal entries

B. Mass upload of recurring journal entry templates

C. Available released APIs, migration objects, or public-cloud-compliant integration options

D. Recommended best practices followed by other customers facing similar requirements

Has anyone successfully implemented a scalable solution for this scenario in SAP Public Cloud?Any guidance, recommendations, or alternative approaches would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you in advance for your support.
